summary: Defines an anonymous login mechanism for the SASL framework. Since plain text logins are not allowed in new IETF protocols, a standard way is needed to log in as an anonymous guest. It was replaced by RFC 4505.

eli5.summary: Sometimes you need to enter a place without giving your name. This is the rule for logging in as a guest safely.

questions: how to log in anonymously with sasl
subtitle: Standard way to log in as a guest in SASL protocols

tldr.problem: Many Internet services need to allow anonymous access, but old protocols used unencrypted plaintext logins. New IETF protocols cannot use plaintext, so a standard way to request anonymous access was needed.
tldr.mechanism: The ANONYMOUS mechanism for SASL lets a client send optional trace information (an email address, an opaque token, or nothing) in a single message. The server may log the trace for accounting but grants access with restrictions.
tldr.outcome: Replaced by RFC 4505, this standard ensured anonymous access worked safely in SASL-based protocols like IMAP and SMTP.

today: RFC 2245 was replaced by RFC 4505. It remains an Internet Standard specification for SASL anonymous access.

sections.title: The Need for Anonymous Access
sections.content:
Anonymous access is common on the Internet: public archives, guest accounts, test services. Older systems allowed login with the user name "anonymous" and a plaintext password. Since new IETF protocols forbid plaintext authentication, a standard mechanism within SASL was needed.

The ANONYMOUS mechanism lets a client claim guest access without a password. It is simple and requires no encryption because it sends no secrets.
sections.eli5: Some services let anyone log in without a password. This is the safe, standard way to ask for that in new Internet protocols.

sections.title: The ANONYMOUS Message
sections.content: The client sends a single message with optional trace information: an Internet email address, an opaque identifier of up to 255 characters with no '@' sign, or nothing. The trace is not authenticated, so it can be false, but the server can log it for debugging and auditing. This is designed so users can stay private (send nothing) or provide a contact for abuse reports (send an email).
sections.eli5: You can send nothing, or a fake name, or a real email address so someone can contact you if you cause trouble. The server logs whatever you send.

sections.title: Security and Best Practices
sections.content: Anonymous access opens security risks. Servers should disable it by default and restrict anonymous users: limit their resource use, forbid write access (or use a drop-box model), set idle timeouts, and disable expensive operations. The trace information is not authenticated and can be forged to frame other users, so administrators should not rely on it for blame. Encryption and external integrity checks are encouraged.
sections.eli5: Letting anyone in is risky. Servers need to limit what guests can do and watch for abuse. The trace info can be faked, so do not trust it to identify someone.
